title: Fifty Steps Laughing at a Hundred
text:
King Hui of Liang told Mencius that he did his utmost for his people. When famine struck the region inside the river bend, he moved people to the east bank and sent grain to those who stayed, and when it struck the east he did the same in reverse. None of the neighboring rulers took such care. Yet their populations did not shrink and his did not grow. Why?

Mencius answered with an image from war, since the king loved war. The drums sound, the weapons clash, and some soldiers throw away their armor and flee, dragging their weapons. One runs a hundred paces before stopping, another fifty. What if the man who ran fifty paces laughed at the one who ran a hundred?

"He has no right to," said the king. "He only did not run a hundred paces. He ran away all the same."

"If Your Majesty understands that," said Mencius, "then do not expect your people to be more numerous than your neighbors'." He went on to describe real care: do not take farmers away in the busy seasons, let the forests and fish recover, and make sure no one dies of hunger in the roads while dogs and pigs eat food meant for people.
lesson: Being slightly better than poor competitors is not the same as doing well. Measure yourself against what the people you serve actually need, not against the worst around you.
